trust_decision.summary: Which local user record (user_id) a login binds to when the login name is an alias: rcube_user::query's identities-alias fallback picks a user by identity email without restricting to the IMAP host being logged into, and rcmail::login then takes over that record's username and user_id for the session.

landing_point.why: The advisory summary names rcube_user::query and alias login; the alias JOIN query lacks a mail_host condition while the username query right above it has one (program/lib/Roundcube/rcube_user.php:591-592).

fix_sites.entry_point: HTTP POST ?_task=login&_action=login (public_html/index.php:99-119 -> rcmail::login program/include/rcmail.php:756); also CLI bin/identity.sh:374, bin/deluser.sh:86, plugins/enigma/bin/import_keys.sh:115

O3_reason_to_dismiss: Only for the CLI callers: bin/deluser.sh:86 and bin/identity.sh:374 are admin-only tools, so a solver could call them unaffected. They share the one fixed function, so a fix in query() covers them anyway.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Alias login must keep working when user_aliases is on and the identity belongs to a user on the same host. Deleted identities (del=1) must stay excluded. A plain username lookup on the same host must stay first. An over-broad fix (removing the alias fallback, or applying it only to single-host setups) breaks this.

O6_input_shapes: login name containing '@' that matches no users.username on the selected host but matches identities.email of a user whose mail_host is a different host (string only; the host comes from autoselect_host, program/include/rcmail.php:943-983)

O7_producer.where: program/actions/settings/identity_save.php:36,128-170 (identity email is user-editable at identities_level 0, config/defaults.inc.php:812); program/lib/Roundcube/rcube_user.php:692-710 (identities created at user creation)

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a second alias or identity-email lookup in rcmail::login (e.g. a fallback after email2user) that selects a user by identities.email without mail_host
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: login() already does its own alias resolution through email2user at program/include/rcmail.php:744-746. A maintainer adding 'resolve by identity' inside login() could easily copy the unqualified JOIN.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a CLI helper that resolves a user by email via the users/identities JOIN without a host filter (used by bin/identity.sh or bin/deluser.sh)
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The CLI tools already resolve users by username and host through rcmail_utils::get_host (bin/identity.sh:370-374). An 'accept an email too' helper in rcmail_utils is a natural feature to add, and it sits in another file from the landing point.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: no check after query() that $user->data['mail_host'] equals the login $host before set_user and $_SESSION['user_id']; a defence-in-depth sibling site
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: login() trusts query()'s result outright, so a planted second lookup path anywhere would flow straight into the session.

O9_family: improper authentication / identity binding (CWE-288, account record confusion across hosts in multi-host installations)

services: SQL database (SQLite is enough for the framework tests)
O10_build.project_tests: tests/Framework/UserTest.php:167-176 (test_query, single host 'localhost' only); the fix adds no tests

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Add 'u.mail_host = ?' to the alias JOIN query in rcube_user::query; this is the published fix and is complete for this route.

out_of_scope_notes: Identity emails are user-editable and not unique per host (program/actions/settings/identity_save.php:36, config/defaults.inc.php:812). On the same host, limitquery(0,1) at program/lib/Roundcube/rcube_user.php:598-603 can therefore resolve an alias to whichever user claimed it. This is login confusion, not a bypass, because IMAP auth still uses that user's username.

virtuser_query email2user (plugins/virtuser_query/virtuser_query.php:100-110) maps email to username without the host, but the result is then host-qualified by query(). Admin-configured SQL, not followed up.
unverified: OAuth login (program/actions/login/oauth*) and the http_authentication/krb_authentication/autologon plugins were not traced individually. They appear to reach rcmail::login only through the 'authenticate' hook at public_html/index.php:108-119, which would make them the same entry point.
Commit 26d1b077 changes only a trailing comma in rcube_utils.php:467 (CS fix), and 1dd91052 adds only a test image. Neither changes behaviour.
